properties.name: Snapshot the five-increment plan before correcting its "stop after any of" claim
properties.rationale:
⭐ THE PLAN'S OWN SELLING POINT IS WHAT FAILED, AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY DONE. "Stop after any of" was the argument for the ordering — it is what made the plan safe to approve, and it is repeated in three PR bodies. A reader who takes it at face value at increment 4 will start a step they cannot finish or ship.

🛑 HOW IT WAS MISSED WHEN THE PLAN WAS COSTED. The scoping measured each crate's SIZE and each crate's IMPORT COUNT, and it measured the dependency direction between crates (storage depends on core, which is why core was ordered first). What it never asked is whether the two share TYPES ACROSS THE BOUNDARY — a re-export is invisible to a line count and to a dependency arrow alike. **A dependency graph tells you what needs what to build; it does not tell you what breaks if you take one and not the other.**

⭐ AND IT WAS FOUND BY SCOUTING BEFORE WRITING CODE, which is the only reason it cost nothing. The increment-4 scout ran the multiline-aware import scan — the one whose absence caused the increment-3 error — and it surfaced two sites importing `Value` through `dynograph_storage` rather than `dynograph_core`. Two files out of eighty-six. **The signal was two lines wide and it invalidated a five-step plan.**

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: increments 1-3 shipped and are genuinely independent; three of six crates are gone and no new external crate entered the tree. The stopping point the plan named after increment 3 is real and was reached.
properties.subject: record
properties.summary:
`dec:absorb-the-foundation-subset-and-end-the-dependency` promises "five increments, each independently shippable, stop after any of". **That is true for 1, 2 and 3 and FALSE for 4 and 5.** They are one increment, and the plan is corrected to say so.

MEASURED, not reasoned: `dynograph-storage/src/lib.rs:32` re-exports `pub use dynograph_core::{DynoError, Schema, Value}`, and `StoredNode.properties` is `HashMap<String, Value>` of that same type. So absorbing `dynograph-core` while `dynograph-storage` remains an external dependency gives reflow2 TWO distinct types called `Value` and TWO called `DynoError` — the in-tree ones, and the ones every `StorageEngine` call keeps returning. 48 reflow2 files name `DynoError`, 33 name `Value`. Nothing would compile.

NO ORDERING AVOIDS IT. Storage cannot go first: it DEPENDS ON core. Keeping the absorbed core unused until storage lands is not absorbing anything. The only honest options were to merge the two or to stop after increment 3.

COMBINED SCOPE: ~5,516 lines (core 1,941 + storage 2,728 non-test + text 847), ~86 importing files, and it brings **rocksdb** and **tantivy** into reflow2's own manifest along with rmp-serde, lru, serde_yaml, uuid and thiserror.
